# An `open` claiming a guid the book has given to another account.
#
# The exporter writes `guid:` on every `open` so an account keeps its identity
# across a round trip, and the importer refuses a guid another object already
# holds — otherwise two accounts would answer to one name in every file that
# refers to either. Re-importing an export taken before an account was renamed
# in GnuCash is exactly that: the file says `open Assets:Bank` with the guid
# the book now has on `Assets:Chequing`.
#
# The refusal comes after the account is attached to the tree, and the
# business-objects pre-pass swallowed it: the account stayed, without the
# identity it was refused, and the pass that would have reported the failure
# found the account already there and said nothing. `Errors: 0`, exit 0, and a
# second account answering to a freshly minted guid.
#
# What this fixture produces: a refusal naming the guid, and no account by
# that name.
#
# Verified by tests/integration/test_an_open_that_fails_after_it_is_attached.py.
2026-01-01 commodity CAD
	mnemonic: "CAD"
	fullname: "Canadian Dollar"
	namespace: "CURRENCY"
	fraction: 100
2026-01-01 open Assets
	guid: "aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa0001"
	type: Asset
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
2026-01-01 open Assets:Chequing
	guid: "aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa0002"
	type: Bank
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
2026-01-01 open Assets:Bank
	guid: "aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa0002"
	type: Bank
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
